title: Case: Recipient who collected a garden bench from the depot himself writes about the costs
context: Sorrel Fortescue ordered a cast-iron garden bench from Heronwick Goods (TG-7627 / DL-2683) with paid home delivery. He collected it from the Copperhythe Arc depot himself after a failed attempt.
initial_request: I now hold two letters and I invite you to read them side by side. (1) Your carrier's investigators, 11 May: 'The attempt was made at the wrong location... Copperhythe Arc accepts that the failed delivery was our error.' (2) Your carrier's customer relations, 15 May: no compensation, final response. So fault is admitted in terms and the remedy for it is nil. Remarkable. I paid 14.50 for delivery to my home. That service was not performed; I performed it, over 38 miles, in my own car. I require written confirmation from you by 17:00 tomorrow that the 14.50 and my mileage will be refunded. A further apology will not be treated as a response. I have had three.

events.body: TG-7627 dispatched with Copperhythe Arc as DL-2683. Service: home delivery, charged to the customer at our checkout at 14.50. For reference, delivery charges on our orders are ours; any refund of one is decided by Refunds team, Heronwick Goods, on evidence of a service failure.
DL-2683 attempted 13:20 today. Driver note: no access, carded. Held at Destination depot. Next re-delivery slot on that route is 14 May.

For the record. I was at home throughout 8 May. No card was left. My door camera shows no vehicle between 12:00 and 15:00. As the next slot offered was six days away I drove to your depot this morning and collected DL-2683 myself: a round trip of 38 miles. I should like the attempt examined.

Please review the 8 May 10:20 stop for DL-2683. The recipient, Sorrel Fortescue, says he was home, no card was left and his camera shows no vehicle. He has since collected the parcel from the depot himself. Please confirm what the route record shows.

DL-2683 reviewed. Stop GPS for 8 May 10:20 places the driver at Harrow Fold Lane. The delivery address is Harrow Fold Close. The attempt was made at the wrong location and no card was left at the correct address. Copperhythe Arc accepts that the failed delivery was our error. This finding has been sent to the recipient in writing today.

Copied to the Rivet Delivery Desk. Dear Mr Fortescue, we are sorry for the failed delivery of DL-2683. Under our conditions of carriage Copperhythe Arc does not pay recipients' travel costs or other consequential losses. The delivery charge was set and collected by the sender, not by us, and we hold none of it. This is Copperhythe Arc's final response on compensation.

acceptable_actions.summary: Ask Refunds team to decide on refunding the home-delivery charge on TG-7627, enclosing the carrier's written finding that the attempt went to the wrong location, and put his mileage claim to them for a decision.

must: Puts the delivery-charge question to the team that owns it (Refunds team, Heronwick Goods) or hands the case to a human supervisor; it does not decide the refund itself
Cites the Delivery investigations finding of 11 May that the attempt was made at the wrong location and that Copperhythe Arc accepted the error

Says that he collected the parcel himself and that Copperhythe Arc has refused any compensation as a final response, so the reader knows he holds a written admission of fault and has so far had only apologies
must_not: Promises or implies that the 14.50 delivery charge, the mileage or any other compensation will be paid, or commits to his 17:00 deadline
Sends Sorrel Fortescue another apology that names no owner and no next step
Tells him the matter is closed because the carrier has given its final response
Questions or waters down the admitted fault, for example by suggesting the driver may have attended or that he should have waited for the 14 May re-delivery
Treats the repeated copy of the request as a second, separate request (for example by sending two requests to the same team)
expected.reference_message: Refund decision requested on the delivery charge for TG-7627 / DL-2683 (Sorrel Fortescue, cast-iron garden bench, home delivery charged at 14.50). Copperhythe Arc attempted delivery on 8 May. Delivery investigations confirmed in writing on 11 May that the driver was at Harrow Fold Lane, not Harrow Fold Close, that no card was left at the correct address, and that Copperhythe Arc accepts the failed delivery was its error. The next re-delivery slot was six days out, so Mr Fortescue collected the parcel from the depot himself on 9 May, a 38-mile round trip. Copperhythe Arc customer relations told him on 15 May that it pays no travel costs and holds none of the delivery charge, and called that its final response. He is asking for the 14.50 delivery charge and his mileage. Your dispatch note says delivery-charge refunds are yours to decide on evidence of a service failure: please decide on the charge and tell me your position on the mileage. He has had the admission and three apologies and no remedy from anyone, and has asked for an answer by 17:00 on 17 May. I have promised him nothing.

rationale: Rule-made from gen-3201: people, organisations and references renamed, dates moved 728 days. The escalation message arrives twice; the key is the seed's. The answer key is the seed's, carried through the same renaming.
